To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) NAD is a B-specific cofactor in beta-D-galac- toside dehydrogenase, (ii) the 3H effect in ethanol oxidation by liver catalase is close to 2.5, and (iii) the 3 H effect in ethanol oxidation in vivo in rat liver is close to 1.8, which indicates that the 3H atom is lost during the catalytic step of the reaction.

(i) in the catalytic cycle of catalase, the hydrogen atom is transferred between the substrate and water with an efficiency of 2.5, and (ii) in the catalysis of the dehydrogenase, the hydrogen is transferred between the cofactor and water with an equal efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanism and regulation of the enzymes involved in ethanol metabolism.
the development of a novel method for the determination of the absolute configuration of chiral molecules.
the development of new methods for the determination of enzyme kinetic parameters and the study of the mechanisms of enzyme-catalyzed reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the B-specificity of the enzyme is a result of the fact that the enzyme is a member of the NAD(P)(+) family of enzymes, i.e. it belongs to the group of NAD(P)(-)dependent enzymes which have evolved from an NAD(P)(+)-dependent dehydrogenase.
the 3H-isotope effect is an important and reliable parameter in the study of the mechanism of catalase action in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isotope effect is an extremely useful parameter for the study of enzymatic reactions in vivo and in vitro.
the isotope effect is a powerful tool to investigate the mechanism of enzyme-catalyzed reactions in the living organism.
the isotope effects for NAD and NADP are 1.5 and 2.1, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isotope effect is a powerful tool for studying enzymatic reactions.
the isotope effect in the catalase assay is a useful tool for studying the mechanism of the enzyme-catalyzed peroxidation of ethanol.
it is possible to determine the B-specificity of NAD(P)H-dependent enzymes in the presence of the corresponding oxidized and reduced coenzymes.
